extracted.intended_audience: Biomedical researchers and data scientists interested in NHLBI TOPMed program participation, data access, and use
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize the TOPMed program's goals, data types, infrastructure, study-design expectations, and intended scientific outcomes so researchers can align proposals, data-use plans, or collaborations with NHLBI priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program goal: generate scientific resources for heart, lung, blood, and sleep disorders and advance precision medicine
rubrics_metrics.description: The goal of the TOPMed program is to generate scientific resources that will improve the understanding of heart, lung, blood, and sleep disorders and advance precision medicine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precision medicine is defined as an approach that considers the unique genes and environment of each patient. The program's output should enable improved prevention and treatment by supporting research that furthers understanding of these conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary data types collected: whole-genome sequencing and other -omics
rubrics_metrics.description: The TOPMed program collects whole-genome sequencing and other -omics data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In biology, -omics refers to measurable differences or changes in biological molecules, such as genes, metabolites, proteins, and RNA. TOPMed studies collect multi-omics modalities to enable integrated analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of -omics with molecular, behavioral, imaging, environmental, and clinical data
rubrics_metrics.description: The program will integrate -omics data with molecular, behavioral, imaging, environmental, and clinical data to improve the prevention and treatment of heart, lung, blood, and sleep disorders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful use of TOPMed resources involves integrating genomic and multi-omics measurements with rich phenotypic and environmental/contextual data from parent studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with NHLBI Precision Medicine activities and complementary programs
rubrics_metrics.description: The TOPMed program supports the NHLBI Precision Medicine Activities and complements the All of Us Research Program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals and uses of TOPMed data should align with NHLBI's Strategic Vision objectives, and may synergize with broader precision-medicine cohorts like All of Us.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage new technologies and data science to address origins and individual differences
rubrics_metrics.description: The program leverages new technologies and advances in data science to promote discoveries about the earliest origins of diseases and individual differences in disease processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis is on using cutting-edge sequencing, computational, and analytic methods to discover mechanisms and heterogeneity in disease.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ancestral diversity and scale as program metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: TOPMed consists of over 180,000 whole-genome sequences, of which around 60% are of predominantly non-European ancestry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale and ancestry diversity are explicit program strengths; research leveraging TOPMed should consider and, where appropriate, exploit this diversity to study health differences among populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breadth of -omics modalities collected
rubrics_metrics.description: TOPMed program studies are collecting -omics data—metabolic profiles, epigenetics, and protein and RNA expression patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations should consider which -omics modalities are available for their phenotypes of interest and design analyses to integrate these molecular layers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage of NHLBI clinical and population parent studies
rubrics_metrics.description: The TOPMed program is leveraging data from NHLBI’s clinical and population studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TOPMed genomic data are linked to extensive parent-study phenotypic data (risk factors, subclinical measures, outcomes); effective research plans use these linked phenotypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample eligibility: well-defined clinical phenotypes and outcomes from earlier NHLBI-funded studies
rubrics_metrics.description: TOPMed is collecting whole-genome sequencing data for individuals who have well-defined clinical phenotypes and outcomes from earlier NHLBI-funded studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection emphasizes samples with high-quality, well-characterized phenotypes and outcomes to enable robust genotype-phenotype analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of varied study designs to increase analytic power
rubrics_metrics.description: TOPMed currently consists of data from over 85 different studies including prospective cohorts, case-control studies, extended family structures, and population isolates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different designs confer different advantages: prospective cohorts provide incident cases and risk factors, case-control studies provide many prevalent cases, and family structures/population isolates improve power for rare variant detection—analyses should exploit these design-specific strengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data access and computational infrastructure: dbGaP access and NHLBI BioData Catalyst (BDC)
rubrics_metrics.description: TOPMed genomic data and the pre-existing parent study phenotypic data are available in the NHLBI BioData Catalyst (BDC) ecosystem to researchers granted access through the NIH Database of Genotypes and Phenotypes (dbGaP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BDC is a cloud-based ecosystem providing tools, applications, and workflows in secure workspaces where researchers can find, access, share, store, and compute on large-scale datasets hosted in the ecosystem or that researchers bring to it. Access requires granted dbGaP permissions and use of secure workspaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program success metric: scientific outputs (publications and abstracts)
rubrics_metrics.description: TOPMed has contributed to research published in almost 150 publications and posted over 200 abstracts at numerous professional meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program impact is measured in part by peer-reviewed publications and conference dissemination; proposals and projects should plan for timely, open scientific communication consistent with NHLBI expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium structure and centralized coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: The TOPMed program consortium includes many centers, including the Administrative Coordinating Center and the Informatics Research Center (also referenced: Data Coordination Center) that serve the entire TOPMed program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TOPMed is a multi-center consortium model; collaboration with and use of consortium resources/centers may be expected. The program may expand to include additional centers as it grows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desired scientific contributions/outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The program may lead to future scientific discoveries such as: treatments tailor-made to individual patients that shed light on racial and ethnic health disparities; new ways to screen, diagnose, and treat patients by studying genetic underpinnings; biomarkers that alter risk; interactions between environment and genes; potential targets for new treatments; new ways to define disorders or subtypes based on molecular signatures; targeted ways to develop and test personalized treatments; advances in predicting, preventing, diagnosing, and treating disorders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research using TOPMed should be designed to enable one or more of these outcome types—mechanistic insights, biomarker discovery, therapeutic target identification, refined disease taxonomy, or strategies for personalized prevention and treatment—especially where linked to population diversity and clinical phenotypes.
